scope: Local isolated SQLite WAL / in-process ASGI, not a production MySQL/network capacity test

fixed.issue: Settings borrows a second pooled database connection while retaining its first
fixed.evidence: 32-concurrency warm batch had 5 HTTP 500 responses; one-connection regression reproduced QueuePool timeout
fixed.change: Read storage configuration after releasing the request connection and before starting storage totals

fixed.issue: Concurrent cache misses rebuild the same family snapshot repeatedly
fixed.change: Serialize family rebuilds with shared-data-directory locks and re-read the snapshot after acquiring the lock

fixed.issue: Episode list performs per-row artwork, ancestor state, sharing and preview queries
fixed.evidence: 30-row episode page: 308 SQL statements per request before, 11 after
fixed.change: Batch load page ancestors and artwork; cache absent states and flags within the request

remaining.cause: Full watch interval traversal on every request; held database cursor and Python aggregation
remaining.recommendation: Maintain daily and lifetime summaries with explicit invalidation; display device list independently of watch statistics

remaining.cause: Materializes all matching items and builds ID lists before Python aggregation
remaining.recommendation: Use SQL aggregate expressions and subqueries, preserving current per-item duration rounding and visibility rules

consistency_checks: Only 5 of 16 simultaneous 100-byte reservations accepted with 500 bytes available; other 11 correctly returned 507
16 duplicate writes of the same chunk advanced the offset only once
limitations: Single-process ASGI with threaded handlers; shared-lock behavior across multiple API processes was not separately load tested
No production data or production service was changed
No actual OSS transfer, WAN latency, CDN, proxy, or MySQL capacity test
Before quota 507 responses are recorded in the raw error field; these are expected rejections, not failures
deployment: Working-tree changes only; not committed or deployed
